title: $\otimes^{\mathrm L}$ preserves bounded constructible complexes ($\ell$-adic $\Lambda$)
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be one of $\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline E$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite;
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) or $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]), and let $X$
be a scheme of the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K,L\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ are bounded
constructible ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is
$K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}L$ ([sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]).

external.place: For $K$ and $L$ bounded constructible it is derived $\varpi$-complete (Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8), and its reduction is $$ (K\otimes^{\mathrm L}L)/\varpi\cong(K/\varpi)\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_E/\varpi}(L/\varpi). $$ This is a derived tensor product of bounded constructible étale complexes over the field $\cO_E/\varpi$, hence bounded with constructible cohomology.

For $K$ and $L$ bounded constructible it is derived $\varpi$-complete (Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8), and its reduction is $$ (K\otimes^{\mathrm L}L)/\varpi\cong(K/\varpi)\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_E/\varpi}(L/\varpi). $$ This is a derived tensor product of bounded constructible étale complexes over the field $\cO_E/\varpi$, hence bounded with constructible cohomology.

proof.text: First record the geometric hypothesis needed for detecting cohomology on strata. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian. Since $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. In particular it is quasi-compact, and the constructibility condition in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] is given by a finite stratification.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; finite-type hypothesis from the setting

proof.text: We first treat constructible module sheaves $F,G$ in degree zero. Intersect their finite stratifications, using [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] to form the intersections as fibre products of the actual strata. On each resulting stratum $T$, if $\{U_i\to T\}$ trivializes $F$ and $\{W_j\to T\}$ trivializes $G$, use the cover $\{U_i\times_T W_j\to T\}_{i,j}$: base change of the second covering covers each $U_i$, and composition with the first covering covers $T$. The local models pull back along both projections, since inverse image preserves constant sheaves, tensor products and the pulled-back coefficient ring as below. Thus on every chosen covering object $V$ the sheaves become $R\otimes_A P$ and $R\otimes_A Q$, where $R=\Lambda_V$, $A=\Lambda(*)$ and $P,Q$ are finitely presented $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] the restrictions to strata and covering objects are exact inverse images with the inverse-image coefficient ring equal to $\Lambda_V$. Consequently they commute with cohomology. Their derived tensor comparison is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; since the module inverse images are exact, their derived functors are their termwise functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. It therefore suffices to compute the tensor of these local models, and later to detect vanishing and constructibility on these strata. For comparison with the exact master target categories, local finite presentation there means a cokernel of an arbitrary map between finite free coefficient modules; it does not by definition require scalar matrix entries. On each Noetherian stratum, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] for $\underline E$, and [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality] for $\underline{\Qlb}$, turn precisely those presentations into pro-étale locally finite free modules. Such a module has a finite constant local model with $P=A^r$. Conversely every finite constant local model over either scalar field is finite free, and therefore locally finitely presented in the master sense. Hence for these two target coefficient rings the stratified constructibility conditions, and their bounded full derived subcategories, agree. This comparison uses these separate field-specific statements, not a general identification of local finite presentation with scalar constant models. The integral case of the present item continues to use its stated finite constant local models; no integral comparison theorem is asserted here.

proof.text: For integral coefficients set $A=\mathcal O_E$ and choose a uniformizer $\varpi$. The ring $A$ is a DVR, hence a PID, and each nonzero scalar is a unit times a power of $\varpi$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. For a finitely presented $A$-module $P$, choose a finite free surjection $A^n\twoheadrightarrow P$ and put $N=\ker(A^n\to P)$. Apply [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form] to the submodule $N\subseteq A^n$. Every diagonal scalar is nonzero, since its basis vector has nonzero image under the inclusion; its exponent in the uniformizer factorization is nonnegative because the scalar belongs to $A$. Taking the cokernel of its diagonal inclusion expresses $P$ as a finite direct sum of $A$ and $A/\varpi^a$, $a\geq1$; a unit diagonal gives a zero summand, which is discarded. The same applies to $Q$. Right exactness of the ordinary tensor product then gives corresponding decompositions of the local sheaves into $R$ and $R/\varpi^aR$.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and proof of Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite projective resolutions; diagonal decomposition from the cited Smith normal form statement

proof.text: Multiplication by $\varpi^a$ on the condensed sheaf $\underline{\mathcal O}_E$ is injective: on every profinite set it sends a continuous function $f$ to $\varpi^af$, and $\varpi^af=0$ implies $f=0$ pointwise [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. The functor $p_V^*$ defining $R=\mathcal O_{E,V}$ is an inverse image [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; inverse image of abelian sheaves is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Applying it to this monomorphism shows that multiplication by $\varpi^a$ on $R$ is injective as well. This argument uses the given pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf, rather than substituting the discrete constant sheaf $A$.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, exactness of abelian inverse image; pointwise calculation with the stated condensed coefficient definition

proof.text: For the local integral ring sheaf $R$, the complex $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ is a resolution of $R/\varpi^aR$ by step 4. It is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]: tensoring it with an acyclic complex gives, up to the shift convention, the cone of multiplication by $\varpi^a$ on that acyclic complex, which is acyclic. The unit complex $R[0]$ is also K-flat since tensoring with it is the identity. The K-flat computation of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] therefore computes every local cyclic or free tensor in step 3 using these explicit resolutions.

source.place: Tags 06YN (definition-K-flat) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor); the two-term cone calculation is written out

proof.text:
Tensoring a free summand $R$ with any of the listed summands leaves that summand in degree zero. For two torsion summands, the model of step 5 is
$$
(R/\varpi^aR)\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}(R/\varpi^bR)
\simeq [R/\varpi^bR\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}R/\varpi^bR].
$$
If $a\geq b$ its differential is zero, so both cohomology sheaves are $R/\varpi^bR$. If $a<b$, its cokernel is $R/\varpi^aR$ and its kernel is $\varpi^{b-a}R/\varpi^bR\cong R/\varpi^aR$: multiplication by $\varpi^{b-a}$ gives this isomorphism, since the injectivity proved in step 4 permits cancellation of powers of $\varpi$. For $a<b$, the quotient-sheaf calculation is justified locally as follows: a section of $R/\varpi^bR$ lifts locally to $x\in R$. If $\varpi^a x=0$ modulo $\varpi^b$, refine the cover to write $\varpi^a x=\varpi^b y$; injectivity gives $x=\varpi^{b-a}y$. Conversely every such multiple is in the kernel, and $\varpi^{b-a}y=0$ modulo $\varpi^b$ holds locally exactly when $y=0$ modulo $\varpi^a$. Thus in either case $H^{-1}$ and $H^0$ are $R/\varpi^{\min(a,b)}R$, with no other cohomology. Finite direct sums of these calculations compute the tensor of the local models in step 3. All resulting sheaves have finite constant local models, because $R/\varpi^cR=R\otimes_A(A/\varpi^c)$ and finite sums of finitely presented scalar modules are finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor, explicit two-term computation using steps 3–5

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$, its scalar ring $A=\Lambda(*)$ is respectively the field $E$ or $\Qlb$, by the section formulas of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Finitely presented modules over a field have finite bases; hence the local models of step 2 are $R^r$ and $R^s$ for finite $r,s$. The unit $R[0]$ is K-flat by step 5's identity argument, so their derived tensor is $R^{rs}[0]$. It has a finite constant local model and no cohomology outside degree zero. The calculation applies to the finite-subextension definition of $\underline{\Qlb}$ itself; it does not replace that sheaf by all continuous maps into $\Qlb$.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.8; finite-rank free local calculation with the project coefficient definitions

proof.text: Return to $F\otimes_{\Lambda_X}^{\mathrm L}G$. Exactness and the tensor comparison in step 2 identify the restrictions of its cohomology with those calculated in steps 6–7. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection], cohomology vanishes globally outside $[-1,0]$ in the integral case and outside $\{0\}$ in the rational cases. The hypotheses of this detection statement hold by step 1 and the finite stratification and covering construction of step 2. On each stratum the remaining cohomology sheaves have finite constant local models by the displayed computations, so they are constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Thus the derived tensor of two constructible sheaves lies in the bounded constructible category [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, finite-stratum detection as stated in the cited node; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.8.8 and Proposition 6.8.11(3)

proof.text:
Finally use finite truncation induction, without assuming that a complex itself is locally a constant perfect complex. The standard truncation triangles are supplied by [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For bounded $K$ with top nonzero cohomology in degree $b$, the triangle is
$$
\tau_{\leq b-1}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow H^b(K)[-b]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\leq b-1}K)[1].
$$
Its first term has one fewer possibly nonzero cohomology degree. Derived tensor is exact in each variable [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and the bounded constructible category is triangulated on our Noetherian $X$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. First fix a constructible sheaf $G$: the base case $F[0]\otimes^{\mathrm L}G[0]$ is step 8, shifts preserve the conclusion, the zero complex starts the induction, and the displayed triangle inductively proves $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}G$ bounded constructible. For the second induction fix a bounded constructible $K$ and choose an interval $[c,d]$ containing the cohomology of $L$. The zero object gives the empty-interval case, and a single-degree object $H^d(L)[-d]$ gives the case just proved, shifted by $-d$. For $c<d$, tensor the truncation triangle of $L$ with $K$ to obtain the distinguished triangle $$K\otimes^{\mathrm L}\tau_{\leq d-1}L\longrightarrow K\otimes^{\mathrm L}L\longrightarrow (K\otimes^{\mathrm L}H^d(L))[-d]\longrightarrow (K\otimes^{\mathrm L}\tau_{\leq d-1}L)[1].$$ The first term belongs to the bounded constructible category by induction on $d-c$, and the third term belongs to it by the already proved sheaf case for this $K$. Closure under distinguished triangles gives the middle term. This proves that $K\otimes_{\Lambda_X}^{\mathrm L}L$ is bounded constructible for all three stated coefficient choices.
